newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. gives Panama six choppers for its drug war.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gives Panama six choppers for its drug war.

text.p: The U.S. government gave Panama six helicopters Friday to help in the Central American nation's fight against drugs.

The $5 million donation of UH-1H Bell Textron choppers from U.S. military reserves will be used by Panamanian police to carry out search missions in the remote Darien jungle area bordering Colombia, long a haven for drugs and arms trafficking.

"Panama has a commitment with itself and the international community to combat drug trafficking and related crimes," said President Ernesto Perez Balladares at the ceremony, attended by U.S. diplomats and Panamanian government officials.

The donation is the largest in a continuing anti-drug agreement Panama has with the United States, which includes training for pilots and technicians as well as channelling funds toward drug education programmes, said U.S. Ambassador William Hughes.
